page: Microsoft Azure E96-24as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Easv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz, the CPU includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The server is configured with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96-24as_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU testing, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. Multi-core performance is also strong, with Geekbench multi-core scores in the top 25% and average multi-core stress-ng results. Memory performance is robust, highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score and average memory bandwidth speeds. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier text and image processing speeds, alongside strong prompt processing and top-tier text generation speeds during small-model LLM inference.

The E96-24as_v7 is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory footprints but lower parallel compute requirements, as its constrained-core configuration reduces software licensing costs while retaining access to the full 768.0 GB memory allocation. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a tradeoff for storage-heavy or hardware-accelerated machine learning tasks. This server is best suited for memory-intensive database operations, large-scale caching layers, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
